cards: Diocletian was Roman emperor (r. 284–305 CE) who ended the third-century crisis.
Shapur I was the second king of the Sasanian Empire, who reigned from 241 to 272 CE.
Caracalla was Roman emperor from 198, jointly with his father Septimius Severus and then his brother Geta, and sole ruler from 211 to 217 after having Geta murdered.
Carausius was a Roman military commander of Menapian origin who was given command of the Channel fleet against Frankish and Saxon pirates around 285.
Cyprian was bishop of Carthage from about 249 and one of the most influential Latin Christian writers.
Cassius Dio was a Greek-speaking Roman senator and historian from Nicaea in Bithynia.
Origen was a Christian theologian and scholar of Alexandria and one of the most productive writers of the early church.
Cao Pi was the son of the warlord Cao Cao and the first emperor of the Wei dynasty.
Gallienus was Roman emperor from 253 to 268, first with his father Valerian and alone after Valerian's capture by the Persians in 260.
Constantius I, known as Chlorus, was a Roman emperor of the Tetrarchy, made Caesar in the west under Maximian in 293 and senior emperor in 305.
The Lord of Sipán is the name given to a Moche ruler whose undisturbed tomb was discovered in 1987 at Huaca Rajada near Sipán on the north coast of Peru by the archaeologist Walter Alva.
Maximian was a Roman emperor, raised by Diocletian to be his colleague and ruler of the west, as Caesar in 285 and Augustus in 286.
Philip the Arab was Roman emperor from 244 to 249, born in the province of Arabia in southern Syria.
Plotinus was a Greek-speaking philosopher, born in Egypt, who studied in Alexandria under Ammonius Saccas and from 244 taught in Rome.
Zhuge Liang was the chancellor of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period and chief adviser to Liu Bei, whose alliance with Sun Quan led to victory at Red Cliffs in 208.
Ascaric was a Frankish king who, with Merogaisus, led raids across the lower Rhine into Roman territory at the start of the 4th century.
Claudius Gothicus, or Claudius II, was Roman emperor from 268 to 270, one of the soldier emperors of the third-century crisis.
Endubis was a king of Aksum who reigned around 270 CE.
Saint Eugenios was an early Christian martyr of Trebizond, said to have been executed under Diocletian around 300, and the patron saint of the city.
d. c. 300 · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zürich, a brother and sister said by legend to have been soldiers of the Theban Legion who fled to Zürich and were beheaded there for their Christian faith…
Goi was the eighth king of Baekje, traditionally reigning from 234 to 286.
Gordian II was Roman emperor for about three weeks in 238, jointly with his father Gordian I.
Gordian III was Roman emperor from 238 to 244, raised to the throne at thirteen after the deaths of his grandfather Gordian I, his uncle Gordian II and the senatorial emperors Pupienus and Balbinus.
Januarius (San Gennaro) was a bishop of Benevento martyred around 305, probably in the persecution of Diocletian.
Maximinus Thrax was Roman emperor from 235 to 238, a soldier of humble Thracian origin proclaimed by the army after the murder of Severus Alexander.
Merogaisus was a Frankish king who, together with Ascaric, broke the peace with Rome on the lower Rhine around 306.
Severus Alexander was Roman emperor from 222 to 235, the last ruler of the Severan dynasty, who came to the throne as a boy under the guidance of his mother Julia Mamaea.
Vasishka was a Kushan emperor of the 3rd century CE, one of the successors of Vasudeva I during the empire's decline.
Vasudeva I was the last great emperor of the Kushan Empire, whose inscriptions date roughly from 190 to 230 CE and are concentrated around Mathura.
fl. c. 190–230 CE · Central & East Asia
Emperor Wu of Jin, born Sima Yan, was the founder of the Western Jin dynasty.
Guan Yu was a general of the late Han dynasty and a sworn companion of Liu Bei, founder of Shu Han.
Liu Bei was a warlord of the late Eastern Han who claimed descent from the Han imperial house.
Marcus Aurelius Probus was Roman emperor from 276 to 282, a soldier from Sirmium in Pannonia.
Sima Yi was a general and statesman of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period.
Sun Quan was the founder of the state of Eastern Wu in southern China during the Three Kingdoms period.
Allectus was a Roman usurper who ruled Britain from 293 to 296.
Deng Ai was a general of the state of Cao Wei in the Three Kingdoms period of China.
Dexippus was an Athenian statesman and historian of the 3rd century.
Elagabalus was Roman emperor from 218 to 222, born Varius Avitus Bassianus into the priestly family of Emesa and great-nephew of the empress Julia Domna.
Emperor Xian of Han, Liu Xie, was the last emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty, reigning from 189 to 220.
